auto_update.warning_text: Arch Linux is not designed for fully automatic updates. Kernel updates require a reboot. AUR packages may fail to build without user interaction. Some updates require manual steps (conffiles, DB schemas, etc.). Only enable this if you understand the risks and regularly check your system.
auto_update.auto_install_hint: Runs pacman -Syu on schedule via a systemd user timer. Requires an active polkit agent (Plasma provides one automatically).
module.network.name: Internet
module.network.desc: DNS, TCP optimization, WiFi tuning and speed diagnostics
network.dns_hint: Slow DNS causes delays when opening websites. Fast public DNS (Cloudflare, Google) can significantly improve browsing speed.
network.dns_empty: Enter at least one DNS address
network.tcp_hint: Enables TCP BBR congestion control and optimizes buffer sizes. These are the same tweaks that make Windows networking feel faster. Safe to apply, easy to revert.
network.wifi_hint: WiFi power saving mode reduces speed and increases latency. This is one of the most common reasons Linux internet feels slower than Windows. Disabling it is safe for desktops and laptops plugged in.
network.wifi_powersave_disabled: WiFi power saving disabled (restart may be needed)
network.ipv6_hint: If your ISP does not support IPv6, disabling it can fix connection delays caused by failed IPv6 lookups.
network.speed_hint: Run a speed test to check your current connection. Use it before and after applying optimizations to see the difference.
network.tcp_opt_bbr_desc: Switches from cubic to BBR algorithm. Better throughput on modern connections, especially over WiFi and long distances.
network.tcp_opt_buffers_desc: Increases TCP receive/send buffer limits to 16 MB. Windows uses larger defaults — this matches them.
network.tcp_opt_keepalive_desc: Detects dead connections in ~2 min instead of ~2 hours. Helps with unstable connections.
network.tcp_opt_tweaks: Extra tweaks — Fast Open, MTU probing
network.tcp_opt_tweaks_desc: TCP Fast Open (saves 1 RTT), automatic MTU detection, no slow-start after idle, larger backlog queue.
network.tcp_nothing_selected: Select at least one optimization group
network.drv_hint: Linux WiFi drivers enable aggressive power saving by default. Windows drivers don't — that's why WiFi on Linux is often slower and drops speed until you reconnect. These settings disable the power-saving features that cause the problem. After applying, click «Reload module» to activate immediately, or reboot.
network.drv_applied: Driver config saved (reboot or reload module to fully apply)
network.drv_p_iwlwifi_ps: Disable driver-level power saving — the main cause of speed drops and needing to reconnect
network.drv_p_iwlwifi_uapsd: Disable U-APSD — causes latency spikes and packet loss with some routers
network.drv_p_iwlwifi_11n: Disable HT AMSDU aggregation — fixes packet stalls where data stops flowing
network.drv_p_iwlmvm_scheme: Performance power scheme — keep the radio at full power (1 = active, 3 = power-save)
network.drv_p_rtw88_lps: Disable deep low-power state — fixes random disconnects and slow reconnects
network.drv_p_rtw89_ps: Disable power-save mode — prevents speed drops after idle periods
network.drv_p_ath9k_ps: Disable power saving — prevents speed drops and connection instability
network.drv_p_ath9k_hwcrypt: Disable hardware encryption — fixes connectivity issues with some access points
network.drv_p_brcm_roam: Disable firmware roaming — fixes random reconnects when signal is stable
network.drv_reloading: Reloading WiFi module (connection will drop briefly)...
network.drv_reloaded: WiFi module reloaded — new settings are active
network.drv_reboot_hint: ⚠ Settings in modprobe.d take effect after reboot or module reload. Click «Reload module» to apply now (WiFi will disconnect for a few seconds).
network.drv_nothing_selected: Select at least one driver setting
network.drv_all_optimal: All parameters are already set to recommended values
module.gpu.name: GPU Driver
module.gpu.desc: NVIDIA driver management, diagnostics and status
gpu.confirm_reconfigure:
Reconfigure the GPU driver?

This will detect your GPU and install the appropriate driver. A reboot is required after completion.
gpu.confirm_nouveau:
Switch to the open-source Nouveau driver?

This will REMOVE all proprietary NVIDIA packages and install Nouveau instead.

NVIDIA hardware acceleration, Proton, and CUDA will stop working.
Only use this if the proprietary driver is causing problems.

A reboot is required after completion.
gpu.reboot_warning: ⚠ Reboot required after driver changes to take effect.
